from monitor import is_stuck

# events is list of dicts with keys job_id (str), state (str), at (int)
# now and grace are ints seconds
def test_basic():
    events = [
        {'job_id': 'a', 'state': 'running', 'at': 10},
        {'job_id': 'a', 'state': 'completed', 'at': 20},
        {'job_id': 'b', 'state': 'running', 'at': 5},
    ]
    # now = 0, grace = 0 -> grace not exceeded, should be empty
    assert is_stuck(events, 0, 0) == []
    # now = 30, grace = 6 -> job a latest completed not stuck, job b latest running at 5 < 30-6=24? 5<24 true, so stuck
    # but grace not exceeded? Actually older than grace seconds relative to now? condition: older than grace seconds i.e. at < now - grace
    # with now=30, grace=6, now-grace=24, job b at=5 <24 so stuck
    # test expects stuck b
    assert is_stuck(events, 30, 6) == ['b']
    # test equal grace not stuck
    # now=10, grace=5, at=5 == now-grace? now-grace=5, at=5 not older (strict) so not stuck
    events2 = [
        {'job_id': 'c', 'state': 'running', 'at': 5},
        {'job_id': 'c', 'state': 'running', 'at': 10},  # later running
    ]
    assert is_stuck(events2, 10, 5) == []  # latest running at 10 not older than grace
    # only latest matters
    # job with latest running but equal grace should not be stuck
    events3 = [
        {'job_id': 'd', 'state': 'running', 'at': 5},
        {'job_id': 'd', 'state': 'running', 'at': 5},
    ]
    assert is_stuck(events3, 10, 5) == []
    # job with latest completed never stuck
    events4 = [
        {'job_id': 'e', 'state': 'completed', 'at': 1},
        {'job_id': 'e', 'state': 'running', 'at': 2},
    ]
    # latest completed not running so not stuck even if old
    assert is_stuck(events4, 100, 1) == []
    print('All tests passed')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_basic()
